Why are Presidential Primaries for states spaced over many weeks while the Presidential Election has a vote in all 50 states on the same day?

Becuase the parties ( not the government ) run their primaries and so they get to make the rules since it is their party

Article 2, Section 1 grants the power to Congress to set the election day for all federal elections.

A cursory glance through the history of Presidential Primaries in the US lead me to believe that it's essentially because primaries weren't set up in the Constitution. So states took it upon themselves to figure out how they were going to do it and they came to different conclusions, hence why everything is spaced out so much.

Before National Conventions became the norm, there would just be a caucus of each party's Congressional members to nominate the candidates. Then the Anti-Masonic Party held a convention in 1831 because they didn't have any Congressional members to hold a caucus.

As National Conventions became the norm, delegates were chosen by the individual states as representatives for the conventions, but it wasn't until 1910 that Oregon established a set of rules which required delegates to support the winner of the primary. It wasn't until the clusterfuck 1968 Democratic convention (thanks to the assassination of RFK) that it became a nationwide norm.
Another thing to consider, is the Presidential Candidates had to travel back in the day, to get their message out to potential voters, prior to TV, etc...
